subject: Dedicated fleet: workload telemetry session + sizing artifacts
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
To: Sam Dunn <sam.dunn@helioslabs.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.inference, mina_haddad@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-04-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated fleet: workload telemetry session + sizing artifacts

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the time last week. As we prep a focused sizing session for Helios (aiming to sketch a dedicated GPU footprint and a draft SLA), can you share a short telemetry extract and a few clarifications so we can come prepared? Ideally we get this before our call on Thursday.

Ask list (small attachments welcome):
- Burst windows: 7-day CSV showing per-minute request count (UTC) — we can accept a sampled slice if retention is an issue.
- Session characteristics: average session length, median and p95 requests/session, percent of multi-turn sessions.
- Prompt/response token distribution: typical prompt tokens, average generation tokens, and 95th percentile.
- Model families in use today (e.g., Llama2-70B, mix of open/closed).
- Any special routes that are high-priority for latency (e.g., search rerank, chat assist).

I attached a small schema CSV (helios_telemetry_schema.csv) that lists the columns that are most useful for our sizing engine — if you can drop a file that matches the rows we’ll import it directly into the sizing tool. If extraction is painful, even aggregated numbers (p95 requests/min, mean gen tokens) are fine.

Purpose: we want to size a baseline dedicated pool (GPU SKUs + oversubscription assumptions), call out KV-cache/batching benefits, and identify where we’d recommend separate reserved capacity vs. shared burst.

Proposed next steps:
1) You send sample telemetry + timeframe preferences.
2) We run a quick sketch and share a first-pass capacity diagram 24h before the call.
3) Discuss tradeoffs on the call, then iterate to a commit-ready footprint.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.inference

On 12 Apr 2026, Marcus Lin wrote:
> Hi Sam / Priya,

> Thanks again for the time last week. As we prep a focused sizing session for Helios...

Thanks Marcus — attaching a 48-hour sampled export (minute granularity) and a small CSV with token summaries. We redacted any PII columns. Files attached: helios_telemetry_snapshot.csv, token_dist_summary.csv.

Notes from our side:
- Primary production traffic is US-based with a noticeable evening spike (21:00–23:00 PDT). Peak p95 requests/min ~ 820 (sample window).
- Models: mix of Llama2-13B for majority, a smaller set of Llama2-70B for long-form generation; about 12% of requests hit the 70B family.
- Average prompt tokens: 110; average generation tokens: 380; p95 generation tokens: 1,200.
- Session behavior: ~60% single-turn, ~30% short multi-turn (2–6 turns), ~10% extended sessions.

We can meet Thursday 2026-04-15 at 11:00 PDT — that works for our eng and product leads. If you need a different timeframe, let us know.

Sam
Sam Dunn
Head of Product Operations, Helios Labs
sam.dunn@helioslabs.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>, mina_haddad@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-04-12T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet: workload telemetry session + sizing artifacts

Marcus / Mina — saw Sam’s dump and skimmed the snapshots. A few quick clarifying Qs before we produce the first-pass sketch: 

1) Tokenization: are the token counts in token_dist_summary.csv using the same tokenizer across both model families? If they mixed tokenizers we should normalize to a single tokenization assumption for our per-token cost model.
2) Cold start rate: do you have an estimate of cold KV-cache misses (percent of requests that benefit from a warmed KV cache)? If not, we can assume 30% cold during peak for a conservative sketch.
3) Concurrency expectations: the snapshot shows p95 per-minute; do you have per-second bursts (short windows where traffic spikes inside a minute)? Seconds-level bursts change batching assumptions.
4) Long tail generation: for the 70B family p95 generation tokens at 1,200 is large — do those typically run as asynchronous background jobs or user-facing sync calls (latency-sensitive)?

Assumptions I’m likely to use in the sketch unless you push back:
- Batchable latency-sensitive routes: assume 25–40ms added batching/queueing budget (we’ll show tradeoffs).
- KV-cache benefit: assume warm inference reduces effective compute by ~35% for multi-turn chat-like routes.
- Oversubscription baseline: 2.0x for 13B family, conservative 1.2x for 70B unless you want stronger isolation.

I’ll compile a quick capacity sketch (GPU count + recommended SKUs + cost estimate) and attach it before the Thursday call.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Inference Architect, Redwood Inference
